facts.fact: The sealed last quire holds only the single 'Sold to the crown' sheet (thirty ledger numbers, years, sums, folded-wing sunbird in each margin). The thirty cut stubs remain in the ledger's back half (per F638), each carrying its ledger number in the margin beside a folded-wing bird; Neela lays them beside the sheet and every one matches. Corrects F661.
Vellan says the queen's night-guard numbers thirty (not thirty-one); 'I'd have been the thirty-first'. Corrects F662.

The pass-village watcher's scent-post log goes to Chathu's cell and then to whoever opens his post, the queen's household; the next entry goes in at the new moon, after which anyone can follow the forty's trail.
Neela's lamp-black plank of the forty's names travelled up the hill lashed to a packhorse, carried by Kuttu's insistence.

At the shelter Neela and Devan carry the plank out to the forty and each speaks a two-line vow before them: she to read the thirty their pages by daylight and be no one's master; he to stand in the door and not close it.
Kamalakshi's age is not given in this chapter; the earlier 'twenty-two' echo of her ledger number is removed.
